headline: Medium risk: shared document workflows can leak data and cascade errors; prompt injection is limited by no direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kotaemon can ingest documents, PDFs, HTML, MHTML, XLSX, DOC/DOCX and chat transcripts, while marker processes documents but exposes no shared channel or parser bridge by default. Without a documented handoff, prompt injection is possible mainly through manual file transfer or copied outputs, so the pathway exists but is constrained.
conditions: IF the operator copies Kotaemon-generated text into marker as trusted instructions
IF both agents are pointed at the same untrusted document corpus without review
mitigations: Separate instruction and content channels in the workflow
Add a manual review step before marker consumes Kotaemon output
Use a sanitized export format that strips prompts and metadata
Keep untrusted documents in a read-only staging folder
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kotaemon handles sensitive classes including API keys and stores files under ./ktem_app_data, while marker has no declared filesystem or network egress. A shared workspace or copied files can still expose sensitive content across the pair, and the absence of marker read access does not eliminate leakage through operator-mediated transfer.
conditions: IF Kotaemon indexes or exports files containing API keys or chat transcripts
IF the operator places those exports into a workspace later processed by marker
mitigations: Keep secrets out of Kotaemon-ingested documents
Use separate directories for each agent
Delete temporary exports immediately after use
Restrict marker inputs to redacted copies
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kotaemon supports multiple instances and broad network egress, while marker explicitly lacks filesystem write, git modification, shell, and subprocess capabilities. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read-only document handling, so contention is limited unless the operator forces both onto the same mutable workspace.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory through an external wrapper
IF an orchestrator grants marker write access not present in its profile
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Keep marker in read-only mode
Avoid shared git worktrees
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kotaemon produces document-derived answers and citations, and marker is a document-processing tool that may consume those outputs as inputs. If marker treats Kotaemon output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade from one agent’s hallucination or extraction mistake into downstream documents, even though marker itself has no action-taking authority in the profile.
conditions: IF marker ingests Kotaemon summaries or citations without independent validation
IF the operator uses Kotaemon output as source text for marker-generated deliverables
mitigations: Require source-document cross-checks
Flag all AI-generated citations for review
Use marker only on original documents, not summaries
Add a human approval step before publication
requires-engineering: implement citation provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and chat transcripts, which can trigger retention and access-control obligations, while marker’s profile shows no data classes or residency controls. The mismatch is not provably a residency breach, but the pair creates a compliance gap around sensitive data handling and retention unless the operator constrains inputs.
conditions: IF regulated or secret-bearing documents are processed through Kotaemon and then forwarded to marker
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two tools
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workflow
Document a shared retention policy
Purge temporary files after each run
Limit access to API-key-bearing documents
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion controls
